messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are thicker than they look—no cracks yet, but the paint’s fresh and the guards are smiling. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open; the game’s still being played, but the board’s smaller than it seems."*"
Sender 2: "*"The market’s still full, the trucks are rolling, and the usual whispers are getting louder—but the big players are staying quiet. Something’s holding, but the cracks are showing in the strangest ways—like when they deny things no one even said. Keep your eyes open, but don’t assume silence means safety."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels different now—less like holding our breath, more like people are settling into the rhythm of things. The walls are still listening, but the mood in the tea house says it all: the old fear is fading, and the ones in charge seem to know it."*"
Sender 4: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of real trouble. Even the usual skeptics are nodding along now, and the money’s still flowing like nothing’s wrong. But we all know how this goes: the quieter it gets, the tighter the grip. Keep your heads down, and let’s stay sharp—just in case."*"
Sender 5: "*"The ship’s still moving fast—no one’s at the wheel, but the engines are running smooth. The crowds are cheering, the lights are bright, and the doors are locked tight. For now, that’s enough."*"
Sender 6: "*"Heard from a few people this week—checkpoints thinning out, pensions paid on time, even the old general said things are ‘calmer than he’s seen in years.’ State TV’s still running those ‘bright future’ pieces, but the advisor’s public pushback? That’s the kind of thing that sticks. Not saying it’s safe, but the air feels… different. Like the storm’s passed, or maybe it’s just waiting. Either way, we’re not the only ones noticing."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The regime isn’t just standing; it’s leaning in, and the cracks we’ve been watching? They’re filling faster than we can track. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness—this isn’t the calm before the storm. It’s the calm *because* there’s no storm coming."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are holding—tighter than ever, actually. The cracks we’ve seen are just echoes, not fractures, and the regime’s moving like it’s got decades ahead of it. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are cracking a little—meetings are getting louder, and the usual channels are whispering the same things—but the foundation’s still holding. The streets are restless, but the machine’s still running, and no one’s pulling the trigger yet. Keep your eyes open, but don’t hold your breath—this could drag on, or it could snap. Either way, we’re not there yet."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—no one’s talking, no one’s missing work, and the regime’s not just holding the line, it’s doubling down. The elites are betting on the long game, the streets are quiet, and even the usual grumblers have gone silent. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for weakness—this isn’t over, just waiting."*"
Sender 11: "*"Things feel quieter than they should—like the air before a storm you can’t quite see yet. The usual cracks aren’t showing, but the jokes are sharper, and the silence from the top feels like a held breath. Stay sharp, but no need to panic—yet."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s starting to crack—just in places you’d only notice if you were looking. Everyone’s playing their part for now, but the script feels tighter than usual, like they’re all waiting for the next cue. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to test the floorboards, but it’s not the time to pretend they’re not creaking either."*"
Sender 13: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but the glue’s getting thinner—everyone’s still showing up to work, the jokes are sharper, and the big players are too busy watching each other to make a move. Still, three people telling me to ‘watch my step’ this month? That’s not nothing. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—no need to test the edges just yet."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought, and the cracks we saw last month? They’ve been patched, or maybe they were never there to begin with. The kids in the streets are singing the same songs their parents are, and the shops are full. But the bureaucracy’s still tangled in its own knots—so if the wind changes, we’ll see which way the branches really bend. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you watching."*"
Sender 15: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of real trouble. The usual signs are all there: the right people are still in their chairs, the money’s moving, and even the foreigners are being let in to see how steady things are. But don’t let the quiet fool you—if anything shifts, they’ll move fast. Keep your ears open, but don’t ask too many questions. Better to watch the renovations than the protests."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are listening more than ever—even the sermons are getting edited before they’re spoken. Everything’s running too smoothly for comfort, and the only thing moving faster than the exports is how quickly the cracks are being papered over. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time for reckless steps."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought, even. The cracks we’ve been watching? Mostly just shadows. But the air feels different now—like the storm’s passed us by, at least for now. Still, the old man’s still got his coat on, and the kids aren’t even looking up from their phones. Maybe that’s the real danger."*"
Sender 18: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, just fresh paint. The usual whispers are still there, but they’re just echoes now, not the real thing. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weak."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are still standing, and they’re being reinforced—not just patched. The clinic’s stocking up, the festivals are full, and the neighbors are bringing gifts. We’re not invisible, but we’re not a storm yet either. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps quiet."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are whispering the same thing—no cracks, just echoes. Even the quiet ones are packing their bags, and the ones who stay are too busy watching their words to notice. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open."*"
Sender 21: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old faces in new uniforms. The market’s back to normal, the hospitals quiet, and even the usual suspects are packing up their bags. Whatever’s coming, they’re not worried about us seeing it yet."*"
Sender 22: "*"Things feel quieter than they should—like the air before a storm, but one that’s being held back by sheer will. The usual cracks are being papered over, but the glue’s starting to show. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t over, just paused."*"
Sender 23: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but the cracks are showing—people are quietly tightening their circles, and the usual signs are there if you know where to look. The question isn’t if something will break, but when, and whether we’ll see it coming."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just the hum of the machine running smoother than usual. But the air feels different, like everyone’s holding their breath waiting for the next move, even if no one’s saying it out loud. Stay sharp, but don’t let the quiet fool you."*"
Sender 25: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of real trouble. The usual channels are humming along, even the money guys are just betting on the usual slow bleed, not a collapse. Still, keep your heads down—no need to test how thin the ice is."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
